answer: Each owner gets one marked hull from the old yard, and the mark is struck into the copper below the waterline for good, so a mark is never struck twice and no sibling can wear one already launched. A claim pays only when that hull is let to wander past the harbour mouth and turned at the zenith of the tide under its own copper. The price of a mark is the number of hulls the crowd has already launched, so the crowd's tenth hull costs ten times its first, and a farm cannot split itself to buy in cheap.
